prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D room layout, separating the bright foreground bed on the lower left (0.5–1.8 m away, with its near edge, smartphone, and cables within the camera wearer's arm's reach at 0.5–1.0 m) and the partly cropped aquarium cabinet on the right (1.0–1.8 m) from the carpeted floor passage between them and the dark background walls and closet doors (2.5–3.5 m behind the bed). Across the 5 frames, the black-and-white cat on the left side of the bed turns from facing right at ~1.8 m away in frames 1–2 to facing and walking toward the camera wearer in frames 3–5, brightening as it approaches to ~0.8 m (within arm's reach) while the camera pans slightly left and pushes the right-side cabinet mostly out of view. As the cat advances, its brighter silhouette clearly occludes the small pillow immediately to its left (~1.5 m away) and the glass tank behind the bed (~2.2 m away), and the depth map reveals the 3D separation between the dark cat and the dark background clutter in frames 1–2 where its black fur blends into the shadows in RGB. However, the depth map is unreliable for fine or flat geometry, erasing the smartphone, most of the charging cables on the mattress, and the cat's raised tail in frames 3–5, while bright illumination from the upper-right aquarium distorts its depth into an artificially near plane.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map fails to capture the overall room layout—omitting the foreground bed (0.5–1.8 m away), the phone and cables within the camera wearer's arm's reach (0.6–1.0 m), the right-side aquarium stand (1.0–1.8 m, partly out of view), the dark bag and box by the closet doors (2.5–3.0 m), and all background structures—and produces no masks at all in frames 1, 2, and 5. In frames 3 and 4, it isolates the cat on the left side of the bed (~1.3 m away in frame 3, approaching to ~1.0 m in frame 4 as it turns to face and look toward the camera wearer), and in frame 4 it also segments the small yellow pillow (~1.4 m away, ~0.2 m to the left of and slightly behind the cat) where the cat's body partially occludes the pillow's right side. When active in frame 4, the mask cleanly delineates the cat's upright tail against the cluttered glass tank behind the bed (~2.2 m away), which is harder to separate at a glance in the RGB image. Overall, the map is highly unreliable, missing the cat entirely when it is farther away (~1.8 m) in frames 1–2 or closest (~0.8 m, within arm's reach, partly cropped at the bottom) in frame 5, omitting all room furniture, and misclassifying the yellow pillow as a "banana" in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: Although no people are present in the room, the pose map places a single yellow human body skeleton in frames 1 and 2 on the dark upright bag and clutter situated on the floor in the back-right corner (~2.5–3.0 m from the camera wearer, ~1.0 m to the right of the bed and ~1.0 m behind the right-side aquarium cabinet, well beyond arm's reach). This false skeleton is oriented with its torso upright, its head keypoints above the shoulders appearing to face forward toward the camera wearer, and its lower legs partly occluded by a cardboard box and white cloth at the base of the closet doors. Across frames 3 to 5, as the camera pans slightly left and tilts down toward the approaching cat on the foreground bed (which moves from ~1.8 m to ~0.8 m within arm's reach), the pose detections disappear completely, leaving the map entirely blank. Rather than revealing true human pose that is hard to see in RGB, the pose map is completely unreliable here: it hallucinates a human figure on dark background objects in frames 1–2 and provides no skeletal tracking for the quadrupedal cat or any surrounding scene elements.
